question.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector. The variances of ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ and their correlation coefficient are given by

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{2}=20,\,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=5,\,\rho =-\frac{3}{5}.
$$

Given that the joint probability density function of $X$ is

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{k}\,exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu )^{T}\,{Σ}^{-1}\,(x-\mu )),
$$

where $\mu $ is the mean vector and $Σ$ is the corresponding covariance matrix, find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =(\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}),\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & \rho {\sigma }_{1}{\sigma }_{2} \\ \rho {\sigma }_{1}{\sigma }_{2} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\sigma }_{i}^{2}=\text{Var}[{X}_{i}],$ ${\sigma }_{12}=\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}],$ and $\rho $ is the correlation, then the joint probability density function of $X$ is

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{|Σ|}}exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu )^{T}\,{Σ}^{-1}\,(x-\mu ))
$$

and $|Σ|$ denotes the determinant of $Σ.$

Using the given values of ${\sigma }_{1}^{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}$, and $\rho ,$ our covariance matrix is

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}20 & -\frac{3}{5}\cdot \sqrt{20}\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\cdot \sqrt{20}\cdot \sqrt{5} & 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}20 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
|Σ|=20\cdot 5-(-6)\cdot (-6)=64.
$$

Substituting this value into our expression for the joint PDF, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{64}}exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu )^{T}\,{Σ}^{-1}\,(x-\mu )) \\  & =\frac{1}{16\pi }exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu )^{T}\,{Σ}^{-1}\,(x-\mu )).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $k=16\pi .$
